increment_paragraph: **OPENSSL-FREE-REMAINING-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS (2026-11-21).** The named follow-up recorded by OPENSSL-FREE-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS and appended by OPENSSL-OBJECT-FREES-SILENT-METHOD-CALLBACKS, run with the USER DECISIONS of 2026-11-21 on its decision items: provider dispatch tables "Named premise + built-in source"; QUIC "Stated slot from source"; setters with no 3.5 man page "Admit pinned source". In quirin-provider-openssl the setters of the functions the frees run on objects they free in turn are declared (teardown_slots.qv, 13 setters, 18 slots): RSA_meth_set_finish, DSA_meth_set_finish, DH_meth_set_finish, ENGINE_set_finish_function, ENGINE_set_destroy_function, EVP_PKEY_asn1_set_free, ASYNC_WAIT_CTX_set_wait_fd, EVP_MD_meth_set_cleanup, EVP_PKEY_meth_set_cleanup and (found by the census) EVP_CIPHER_meth_set_cleanup, each from its 3.5 page; and, source-derived from the pinned 3.5.5 release (file and line cited, range since "3.5.5", the checker's new SOURCE_CITATIONS and SOURCE_SLOTS), EC_KEY_METHOD_set_init (which has no 3.5 page either), ENGINE_set_pkey_meths and ENGINE_set_pkey_asn1_meths. The eight frees that run teardown functions state the slots they run and name two new premises (C04.18.9 gains #library and #loaded): openssl_builtin_teardown_functions for the library's own methods, engines and the default, base, legacy and null providers' dispatch functions (read from source: they run in turn only stated slots, ex_data and the allocator hook; a callback run in turn on an object freed in turn is that object's own teardown, reading R6, user-confirmed) and, per the user decision, the one named premise openssl_loaded_module_functions for the providers and engine modules the library loads (an engine the dynamic engine loads included, reading R8, user-confirmed); on the first report the user decided "Both conjuncts", so the loaded premise states that such a function is inert and runs no application callback in turn on an object of the call (quant all #o in #freed: quant all #f in #teardown(#o): #f in #loaded -> #f |-> #inert && quant all #g in #in_turn(#f, #freed | #args | #created): #g in #library | #loaded), while the built-in premise keeps the inert conjunct alone because built-in functions run the application's ex_data free callbacks and allocator hook in turn. EVP_PKEY_free, X509_free and ENGINE_free state every item and drop openssl_unstated_callback_slots. X509_STORE_free, SSL_CTX_free and SSL_free keep it for a CRL's X509_CRL_METHOD free (X509_CRL_METHOD_new registers into its result, which C04.19.3 cannot state) and SSL_free also for the QUIC TLS crypto_release_rcd (SSL_set_quic_tls_cbs is handed a dispatch table); PKCS12_free and EVP_MD_CTX_free release their argument, through which no slot invocation can be read, so they name a released free's statement (#teardown(#o) \ #stated, which entails the free statement: nothing narrowed). SSL_free also states the message and info callbacks the record layer's clear runs on its error path, found by tracing the QUIC free path past quic_impl.c (it runs nothing else unstated). The EX_DATA_AUDIT classes of SSL_free, SSL_CTX_free and X509_STORE_free gain RSA, DSA, DH, EC_KEY and ENGINE. Merged with OPENSSL-INNER-FREES-SILENT-METHOD-CALLBACKS (r46): its fourteen calls that free a key inside (the SSL_CTX_use_* loaders, the PEM readers, d2i_PKCS12_bio, the verify-path calls, and the handshake and I/O calls and SSL_shutdown) would have lost coverage, since a declared setter's functions are #settable and leave the free statement, so each now states the key's nine teardown slots through a borrowed formal (the handshake calls also the digest, cipher and public key method cleanups) beside both teardown premises, keeping its free statement or the handshake's free conjunct for the rest; a checker test pins all fourteen. contracts.lock against the merged base: 13 entries added, 22 changed (the eight frees and the fourteen inner frees), none removed; pinned, library_versions and every other top-level key unchanged; user-crates-load-path.json and quirin-plugin.json gain the 13 bindings. Lean: QCore.PremiseFormula gains the two terms and three formulas; new QCore.OpensslFreeTeardownSlots, audited (24 theorems). Dispatch-table registration and registration into a result: "Yes, new card later" (user decisions 2026-11-21), registered as OPENSSL-DISPATCH-TABLE-SLOT-REGISTRATION and OPENSSL-SLOT-REGISTRATION-INTO-RESULT. No gateway code changed. Not re-measured (premises are metadata, no Fluent Bit or Monkey source calls a new setter, so every new slot's run set is the closed empty set); pinned routes read no user load path, so no move is predicted and measure --declared is deferred to the integrator.

ledger.text: What remains after OPENSSL-FREE-REMAINING-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS (2026-11-21; USER DECISIONS 2026-11-21 implemented: the teardown setters declared, three source-derived; the slots stated at the frees and at the fourteen calls that free inside; openssl_builtin_teardown_functions and openssl_loaded_module_functions named, the latter with both conjuncts; the QUIC free path traced; EVP_PKEY_free, X509_free and ENGINE_free dropped openssl_unstated_callback_slots). Two items moved to their own entries by the user decisions of 2026-11-21 ("Yes, new card later"): the QUIC TLS crypto_release_rcd on SSL_free (OPENSSL-DISPATCH-TABLE-SLOT-REGISTRATION) and a CRL's X509_CRL_METHOD crl_free on the CRL-freeing frees (OPENSSL-SLOT-REGISTRATION-INTO-RESULT). What this entry still tracks is the released-parameter gap: PKCS12_free and EVP_MD_CTX_free release their argument, and a slot invocation reads only a borrowed parameter (C04.19.3), so they state none of their teardown slots and name the released free's statement (quant all #o in #freed: #teardown(#o) \ #stated |-> #inert). DISCHARGE: a vocabulary decision (C04.19.3, gateway rule 12n, with Lean parity) admitting a slot invocation through a released parameter, read before the release as the member form already reads one; then both frees state their slots (the key's nine, and for EVP_MD_CTX_free the digest, cipher and public key method cleanups), name the free statement only for what is left (PKCS12_free: a CRL's method, until OPENSSL-SLOT-REGISTRATION-INTO-RESULT), and EVP_MD_CTX_free drops the premise. Size: small to medium; needs a user decision on the vocabulary.

ledger.title: SSL_CTX_set_client_cert_engine is undeclared: it registers no function and runs the engine's init function
ledger.text: Found by OPENSSL-FREE-REMAINING-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS. The user decision of 2026-11-21 ("Admit pinned source") covers SSL_CTX_set_client_cert_engine, which has no 3.5 page. It was not declared: it stores an ENGINE, not a function (ssl/tls_depr.c:81-94 at 3.5.5), so it is no slot writer, and the engine's finish and destroy functions the context's free runs are stated through the engine slots (engine_st.engine_finish, .engine_destroy) whatever stored the engine. Declaring the setter itself needs more than its retention: it calls ENGINE_init (the engine's init function, engine_st init, whose setter ENGINE_set_init_function is undeclared) and, when the engine has no client certificate function, ENGINE_finish (the finish slot). DISCHARGE: declare ENGINE_set_init_function (ENGINE_add 3.5) and SSL_CTX_set_client_cert_engine (source-derived) with the retention and the init and finish invocations and a library-value premise for built-in engines' init functions. Size: small. Metadata only.

ledger.title: The OpenSSL allocator's free hook runs at every free, and no premise names it
ledger.text: Found by OPENSSL-FREE-REMAINING-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS (provider census). Every OpenSSL free ends in OPENSSL_free or OPENSSL_clear_free, which call the free function an application may install with CRYPTO_set_mem_functions (crypto/mem.c at 3.5.5). It is a global hook, like the ex_data registry, outside #teardown (no method table, provider or engine of a freed object holds it), so no premise of quirin-provider-openssl names it, on any declaration that allocates or frees. DISCHARGE: decide whether to state it (a run-wide registration read from CRYPTO_set_mem_functions calls) or to name a premise on every allocating or freeing declaration, with a vocabulary term for the hook. Size: small to medium. Metadata only.

ledger.title: Read slot registrations from a dispatch table's initializer (SSL_set_quic_tls_cbs)
ledger.text: USER DECISION 2026-11-21 on OPENSSL-FREE-REMAINING-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS: "Yes, new card later". SSL_set_quic_tls_cbs (3.5 page; accepted on a TLS object, rejected on QUIC objects) is handed an OSSL_DISPATCH table whose entries are the application's QUIC TLS callbacks; SSL_free runs its crypto_release_rcd from RECORD_LAYER_clear (ssl/quic/quic_tls_api.c, ssl/record at 3.5.5). A slot registration's callback must be a function pointer parameter (C04.19.3), so no declaration can state it, and SSL_free keeps openssl_unstated_callback_slots for it. DISCHARGE: a vocabulary and gateway change (C04.19.3, gateway rule 12n, with Lean parity) reading a registration's candidates from the dispatch table's initializer (each {id, function} entry under its function id, an open set for a table not initialized from constant entries), then declare SSL_set_quic_tls_cbs with its slots, state crypto_release_rcd on SSL_free (and the handshake's QUIC TLS callbacks on the handshake and I/O calls), and drop that item. Size: medium.

ledger.title: Let a function's result hold a registered slot (X509_CRL_METHOD_new)
ledger.text: USER DECISION 2026-11-21 on OPENSSL-FREE-REMAINING-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS: "Yes, new card later". X509_CRL_METHOD_new (no 3.5 page; crypto/x509/x_crl.c:486 at 3.5.5) stores crl_init, crl_free, crl_lookup and crl_verify into the method it returns, the only writer of a CRL method's crl_free; a slot registration's holder must be a parameter (C04.19.3), so no declaration can state it. X509_STORE_free, SSL_CTX_free, SSL_free and PKCS12_free, and the inner frees SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations, SSL_CTX_set_default_verify_paths and d2i_PKCS12_bio, keep openssl_unstated_callback_slots for a CRL's crl_free until then. DISCHARGE: a vocabulary change (C04.19.3, gateway rule 12n, with Lean parity) admitting resource_callback_slot_registered(result, TAG.FIELD, F) on a constructor, then declare X509_CRL_METHOD_new (source-derived) with its four registrations, state x509_crl_method_st.crl_meth_free at the frees that free CRLs, and drop that item (the frees with nothing else left drop the premise). Size: small to medium.
